title: How Singapore's government-run dating service works
summary: This article explores Singapore's government-run dating service called First Date, established to address the nation's critically low birth rate and declining marriage rates. The service uses a questionnaire-based matching system where participants fill out detailed forms about their preferences, values, and lifestyle, then are matched with compatible partners for subsidized first dates organized by the government.
problem_solved: Singapore's extremely low fertility rate (0.8) and declining marriage rates threaten the country's demographic sustainability
why_valuable: It demonstrates how governments can intervene in personal life to address national demographic crises through structured matchmaking programs
